title: Commitment & Marketplace Billing: Prioritization Rubric and Intake SLAs
creator: Liam O'Connor
description:
Problem statement: We receive a high volume of non-bug customer requests related to pricing commitments, invoicing adjustments, cost allocation, and marketplace billing flows. Current intake is inconsistent across sales and CS, leading to slow responses, duplicate work, and mis-routed asks that require engineering or finance involvement. Goal: define a concise prioritization rubric, SLA-based intake routing, and handoff contract so PM/Sales/Finance/Eng can make fast, consistent decisions and measure throughput.

Scope: inbound customer requests that are non-bug (policy, billing mechanics, invoice formatting, commitment terms, marketplace revenue allocation, marketplace listing/fee questions). Excludes: security incidents, production outages, legal contract drafting (except where it affects billing tooling).

Deliverables:
- A 4-factor prioritization rubric (Customer Impact, Revenue/ARR Risk, Compliance/Legal Exposure, Implementation Effort) with example scoring and thresholds.
- Intake form template (Salesforce/Zendesk/Notion + fields) driving automated routing rules.
- Response SLAs by priority tier (P0/P1/P2) and default owners.
- Routing matrix mapping request-types to owners (Sales Rep -> Finance -> PM -> Eng -> Legal) with escalation paths.
- Dashboard metrics to track throughput, average time-to-first-response, and conversion of requests to billing changes or product work.

Principles & trade-offs:
- Keep rubric simple enough for reps to use under quota pressure (4 factors, 1-5 scale).
- Prioritize revenue and compliance over low-dollar operational cosmetic invoice requests.
- Lean on Finance for one-time invoice work but require a product ticket for recurring or platform changes.
- Avoid engineering time on manual invoice edits unless clear product or compliance impact is documented.

Example scoring guidance:
- Customer Impact: 1 = cosmetic note, 5 = prevents product usage or causes major business disruption.
- Revenue/ARR Risk: 1 = < $500 ARR impact, 5 = > $250k ARR or immediate churn risk.
- Compliance/Legal Exposure: 1 = no exposure, 5 = regulatory violation or contract breach risk.
- Implementation Effort: 1 = < 1 engineer-day or manual Finance step, 5 = > 4 engineer-weeks or complex cross-team effort.

Priority mapping (example):
- P0: Any score with Compliance >=4 OR Revenue >=5 OR Customer Impact >=5 (Immediate SLA: 8 business hours response; owner: Finance + PM on-call)
- P1: Sum of first three factors >=10 and Effort <=3 (SLA: 48 business hours; owner: PM + Finance)
- P2: All other requests (SLA: 5 business days; owner: Sales/Finance with PM oversight)

Routing rules (high level):
- Invoices & one-off billing adjustments: route to Finance (tickets must include invoice number, requested change, GL code if known). Finance resolves if no product change required. If recurring or platform gap identified, Finance creates PM ticket referencing original request.
- Commitments & discounts: route to Sales -> PM review -> Legal if contract language change. Template discounts under $X can be approved by Sales Ops. Any non-template terms escalate to PM + RevOps.
- Marketplace fee/allocation questions: route to Marketplace PM + Finance. If the question is about marketplace listing metadata affecting billing, escalate to Eng for data model changes.
- Cost allocation and internal chargebacks: route to Finance (internal) with Ops CC'd.

Measurement & signals:
- Dashboard KPIs: time-to-first-response, time-to-resolution, % escalated to PM/Eng, average score distribution, monthly volume by category.
- Success criteria for rollout: 80% of inbound requests are triaged within SLA tiers within 30 days of rollout; >30% reduction in mis-routed escalations to Eng in first quarter.

Implementation plan (90 days):
1) Week 1-2: Finalize rubric and intake fields with Finance, Sales Ops, Legal. Create sample filled tickets for training.
2) Week 3-4: Implement intake form in Zendesk + automation rules; add routing matrix to internal Playbook.
3) Week 5-8: Pilot with two enterprise AEs and Finance specialists; collect feedback.
4) Week 9-12: Iterate and ship org-wide; instrument dashboard and run training sessions.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Reps bypass intake to get fast outcomes. Mitigation: short SLA for high-priority routing + Sales Ops enforcement.
- Risk: Overload Finance with manual work. Mitigation: require Finance to create PM tickets for recurring product changes; track manual work hours.
- Risk: Ambiguous scoring leads to inconsistent routing. Mitigation: practical examples and a quick reference one-pager in the Playbook.
